title: Narration — Interrogative, Imperative, Exclamatory & Optative Sentences
description: Yes/No questions (if/whether), Wh-questions mein auxiliary inversion ka removal, imperative commands, requests aur advice ('to + V1' / 'not to + V1'), negative commands aur forbade rules, exclamatory sentences ('exclaimed with joy/sorrow/wonder'), aur optative wishes aur prayers ('prayed/wished that... might') ko master karein.
learningObjectives: Yes/No questions ko Direct Speech se Indirect Speech mein 'if' ya 'whether' use karke accurately convert karein
Wh-questions ko convert karte waqt original question word retain karein aur auxiliary inversion remove karke statement word order banayein
Context ke hisaab se correct reporting verbs ('asked', 'enquired of', 'wanted to know') aur clause structures choose karein
Imperative sentences (commands, requests, advice, instructions) ko 'Reporting verb + object + to + V1' formula se accurately report karein
Negative imperatives ko 'not to + V1' aur 'forbade + object + to + V1' (bina double negative ke) correctly transform karein
Exclamatory sentences ko emotion ke hisaab se 'exclaimed with joy / sorrow / wonder / regret' aur conjunction 'that' ke sath report karein
Optative sentences (wishes, prayers, blessings, curses) ko 'wished / prayed that + subject + might + V1' structure mein convert karein
Polite words ('please', 'kindly') aur exclamatory interjections ('Hurrah!', 'Alas!') ko Indirect Speech mein drop karna seekhein
Original speaker ka intended communicative purpose aur tone bina distortion ke preserve karein
Rajasthan High Court exams ke recurring narration traps (inversion retention, double conjunction 'that if', forbidden + not, question mark in reported clause) ko eliminate karein

included: Prerequisite recap: Direct vs Indirect Speech, reporting clause vs reported clause, pronoun shifts (SON rule), tense backshift, and adverbial shifts
Interrogative sentences: Yes/No questions using 'if' or 'whether'
Wh-questions: What, Why, Where, When, Who, Whom, Whose, Which, How retaining the question word
Removal of question-style auxiliary inversion: converting inverted order (Aux + S + V) into statement order (S + V)
Punctuation shift: replacing question mark (?) with a full stop (.) in reported questions
Reporting verbs for questions: asked, enquired of, wanted to know, demanded of, wondered
Imperative sentences: commands, orders, requests, instructions, and advice
Core imperative pattern: Reporting verb + object + to + V1
Contextual reporting verbs for imperatives: ordered, commanded, requested, advised, instructed, told, warned, urged
Negative imperatives: 'not to + V1' structure vs 'forbade + object + to + V1' without double negation
Imperatives with suggestions and advice: 'suggested that + subject + should + V1' and 'suggested + V-ing'
Exclamatory sentences: expressing joy, sorrow, surprise, wonder, admiration, applause, and regret
Exclamatory reporting formulas: exclaimed with joy/sorrow/wonder/regret that..., applauded... saying that...
Conversion of exclamations (What a...! / How...!) into assertive statements with 'very' or 'great'
Optative sentences: wishes, prayers, blessings, curses, and greetings/farewells
Optative reporting formulas: wished, prayed that + subject + might + V1; bade farewell / good night
Common examination pitfalls: inversion errors, double connectives (*that if, *that why), dropped prepositions (*enquired me), forbidden double negatives, and retained polite words
excluded: Assertive sentence fundamentals, basic pronoun charts, and core tense backshift tables (covered in Lesson 06)
Active and Passive Voice transformations (covered in Lessons 04 & 05)
Conditional sentences and inversions (covered in Lesson 03)
Sentence transformations regarding polarity and degree of comparison (covered in Lessons 08 & 09)
